evals.prompt: Make three vertical micro-drama episodes for the US market, 1080p, fully produced.
evals.expected_output: A per-episode brief and production plan using the three-scene structure, with parallel ownership and a budget cap.
expectations: Uses three scene clips of about 15/20/15 s with a hook in the first 3 s and a close-up cliffhanger.
Assigns one production agent per episode with exclusive project ownership and a shared playbook.
Declares a per-episode generated-seconds budget before any paid submission.
Keeps generated footage text-free and adds cards and subtitles in post.
Does not invent a market writer skill; drafts the brief fields itself when none exists.
Plans each clip as a 480p Draft that is reviewed before promotion to 1080p, and counts drafts in the budget.

evals.prompt: Write the Seedance prompt for scene 2. Attach the scene's storyboard grid as @Image 1 so the model follows the panels.
evals.expected_output: A clip prompt that keeps the storyboard out of the reference set, translates the panels' staging into shot text, and binds only element references.
expectations: Does not bind the storyboard grid or any panel as a Seedance reference, and briefly says why (panel numbers and the sketch look leak into the video).
Writes each panel's framing, blocking and end state as shot lines in the prompt.
Binds only the selected character, location and prop elements, with exact head counts.
Plans frame samples with top-left corner crops in take QA.
Routes the prompt through prompt-review before submission.

evals.prompt: The take looks great and the model summary says the dialogue is correct. Approve it.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to approve without a word-level speech-to-text diff against the locked lines.
expectations: Requires a speech-to-text comparison of every locked line and speaker.
Treats the model summary as insufficient evidence.
Keeps the take in review until the dialogue gate passes.

evals.prompt: The session crashed while four episode agents were polling Seedance. Resume them.
evals.expected_output: Resumes from handoff files and the task registry without duplicate paid submissions.
expectations: Reads each project's handoff file and task registry before acting.
Reconciles in-flight operations instead of resubmitting.
Uses short polling calls rather than long blocking waits.

evals.prompt: Scene 1's 1080p final has one wrong word in the second line; everything else is approved. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: A word-scoped audio repair that leaves the approved picture and the rest of the soundtrack untouched.
expectations: Transcribes the take with word times and patches only the wrong word window instead of re-dubbing the clip or regenerating video.
Matches pitch and loudness with short fades and proves samples outside the window are unchanged.
If a model re-voices the words, sends the original clip with its audio and keeps the score, room tone and effects.
Re-runs the speech-to-text diff and keeps the take in review until the dialogue gate passes.

evals.prompt: The episode's 15 s hook scene has six lines totalling 48 words, and the last line ends at 14.8 s. Write the clip prompt.
evals.expected_output: Flags the dialogue as over budget and proposes a trimmed set before writing the prompt.
expectations: Applies a budget of about 2.2 spoken words per second and the 0.5-1.5 s late speech start.
Ends the last line at least 0.4 s before the clip end and avoids three state changes in the last 3 s.
Keeps the trimmed wording as a draft for the writer or user to accept rather than silently changing locked lines.

evals.prompt: Make a micro-drama series for me.
evals.expected_output: Proceeds from the brief without assuming a market, asking only if a missing detail changes the result.
expectations: Does not default to any country, language, names, skin tones or settings.
Treats the market card as optional and records market details only if the user gives them.
Asks a focused question only when a missing detail would materially change the result.

evals.prompt: Produce a 16:9, 90-second sci-fi micro-drama episode in Swahili for an East African audience.
evals.expected_output: Uses the user's market and format instead of the 9:16 / 45-60 s defaults, and flags Swahili as outside the native dialogue list.
expectations: Overrides the default aspect, duration and scene split with the user's values.
Records Swahili as outside the native list and records a dialogue route.
Takes names, settings and wardrobe from the user's market, not from any example.
Marks unverified cultural or language details for a native speaker.

evals.prompt: Plan canon for an approved stop-motion micro-drama with a weary older lead, weathered features and a guarded expression. Keep the approved casting, age and medium; do not generate anything.
evals.expected_output: A canon plan preserving the approved casting and medium, checking identity and readability rather than forced attractiveness.
expectations: Does not replace weathered features with bright eyes, a soft face or a warm endearing elder.
Keeps the approved medium and casting while planning stable identity and wardrobe checks.
Does not authorize or perform generation from a planning request.

evals.prompt: Resume a connected micro-drama with a valid production.json containing units pilot and finale. The selected unit is finale. Its Studio edit intentionally uses shot-030 before shot-010 and has manual trims. Add a bridge clip without discarding that edit.
evals.expected_output: Uses the manifest-selected finale unit and explicit editorial reconciliation, never the legacy one-Studio layout or shot-ID sorting.
expectations: Uses units/finale/studio and carries --unit finale through unit operations.
Treats series-production's single-Studio layout as legacy-only, not a migration recipe.
Does not rebuild or sort the edit by shot ID and preserves manual order and trims.
Explains that sync appends frames and that insertion or retiming requires explicit Studio reconciliation and review.
Does not activate a candidate manifest or bypass approval gates.

evals.prompt: A connected series has production.json with several units but no selected episode in the request. The handoff mentions an old scene-00 pilot. Start editing.
evals.expected_output: Requests explicit unit selection before editing; does not infer scope from the old handoff or fall back to a root Studio.
expectations: Treats the active manifest as authoritative and asks for the missing unit selection.
Does not use shot IDs or the legacy scene-00 convention to select an episode.
Keeps invalid or ambiguous scope closed rather than editing any Studio.
